s: A company is building a hybrid environment that includes servers in an on-premises data center and in the AWS Cloud. The company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances in three VPCs. Each VPC is in a different AWS Region. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection to the data center from the Region that is closest to the data center. The company needs the servers in the on-premises data center to have access to the EC2 instances in all three VPCs. The servers in the on-premises data center also must have access to AWS public services. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST cost? (Select TWO.)
o: Create a Direct Connect gateway in the Region that is closest to the data center. Attach the Direct Connect connection to the Direct Connect gateway. Use the
Direct Connect gateway to connect the VPCs in the other two Regions.
Set up additional Direct Connect connections from the on-premises data center to the other two Regions.
Create a private VIE.Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the private VIF to the VPCs in the other two Regions.
Create a public VIF. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the public VIF to the VPCs in the other two Regions.
Use VPC peering to establish a connection between the VPCs across the Regions. Create a private VIF with the existing Direct Connect connection to connect to the peered VPCs.
e: A Direct Connect gateway allows you to connect multiple VPCs across different Regions to a Direct Connect connection1. A public VIF allows you to access AWS public services such as EC21. A Site-to- Site VPN connection over the public VIF provides encryption and redundancy for the traffic between the on-premises data center and the VPCs2. This solution is cheaper than setting up additional Direct Connect connections or using a private VIF with VPC peering.
nt: The PDF split option A across two lines, so option B here is just the end of A. The key's A is 'Direct Connect gateway to reach the other Regions' VPCs'. E is the public VIF that gives on-prem access to AWS public services.

w.y: Note: the source split one option across A and B; A and B together form "create a Direct Connect gateway and use it to connect the VPCs in the other two Regions." The LEAST cost way to reach VPCs in three Regions over one Direct Connect connection is a Direct Connect gateway with a private VIF, and access to AWS public services needs a public VIF (the only option offering one also adds a VPN, which is not strictly needed).

o.A: Correct: a Direct Connect gateway lets one connection reach VPCs in any Region (with B, which is the rest of this option).
o.B: This is the second half of option A, not a separate choice.
o.C: Extra Direct Connect connections to each Region cost far more than a Direct Connect gateway.
o.D: A VPN over a private VIF is unnecessary when the Direct Connect gateway already reaches the other Regions.
o.E: Correct: a public VIF gives on-premises servers access to AWS public services over Direct Connect.
o.F: VPC peering is not transitive, so on-premises traffic cannot pass through a peered VPC to reach the others.
